Kinetiq is building the app economy around Hyperliquid.

Elysium is Kinetiq’s new network for the apps that run alongside Hyperliquid’s exchange, targeting roughly 100 times the block space they get on HyperEVM today. 

Block space has been a key bottleneck on HyperEVM. Market makers pay gas on every quote update, so fee spikes mean fewer updates and wider spreads. Few apps beyond staking and lending have taken off.

More room should let market makers keep prices fresh without fees eating into their margins. A maker selling downside protection through an options app on Elysium could then hedge with perps on Hyperliquid. Each of those trades pays the exchange a fee.

HIP-3 let outside teams launch their own markets on Hyperliquid. Elysium could do the same for apps.

‘Whatever it is you’re going through, keep going’

Those were the first words a stranger said to me at the gym last week. A man a few years older than me, who I’d never spoken to before

‘I’ve seen you around man. The last few weeks, something’s changed, I see it in your face. I just wanted to say, whatever it is man, whatever you’re going through, just keep going’

I don’t share much on here, but he was right. The last couple of months have been pretty brutal. A few hits I wasn’t expecting that, well, really fucking knocked me sideways

So obviously, like any sane person, my first thought was: Jesus. It’s that obvious? How miserable do I actually look?

My second was how hard his words hit. At your lowest, the voice in your head that’s always backed you can start to go quiet. And sometimes that’s exactly when you need to hear it from someone else

To be honest, I just froze a bit and said thank you. I didn’t know what else to say really. Just having someone notice had already taken a bit of the weight off. ‘Thank you. It’s not been great, but I’m here. So thank you’

And that was it. He put a hand on my shoulder and walked away

I’ve seen him a few times since. We haven’t spoken, and I’m not sure we have much to talk about. But his words have stayed with me, like that hand never quite left my shoulder

Because if your own belief ever does run out, and god knows life will test it, sometimes all it takes is one person to see you, and believe in you anyway

From one stranger to another, whatever it is you’re going through, keep going

$WGS earnings. Market cap roughly $1.6B. The good: revenue $123M, margins improved to 72%, adjusted profit $8.6M, reimbursements up 5%, genome collection rates improving, and Medicaid coverage expanding. The bad: volume growth slowing, guidance lowered, reimbursement documentation creating delays, and Medicare reimbursement cuts presenting a 2027 headwind. What needs to happen for the stock to recover? The company needs to reaccelerate volume growth, improve reimbursement collection, reduce payment delays, and demonstrate that expanding Medicaid coverage can translate into sustainable revenue and earnings growth. The entire genomics sector has been under pressure, with even $ILMN down roughly 30%. I believe $WGS will start running again when the sector recovers. I’m not increasing my exposure today because I already have enough, but I’m not selling either. If I had less exposure, I would probably be buying more. 

When $WGS reached $100, it got there without any logic. 
There was no meaningful improvement in the underlying business, yet the stock price had doubled. Now it’s being oversold again because of market sentiment and pressure across the entire sector. This is simply the nature of stock market cycles. Prices can become completely disconnected from business fundamentals in both directions. You buy when pessimism becomes excessive and sell when optimism exceeds logic.

The Democratic midterm sweep has raised valid questions about the AI data centre buildout. The reality is more nuanced than the recent market reaction suggests.

2027 capacity looks largely intact. Most projects scheduled to come online next year are already under construction and newly elected governors are not expected to disrupt work that has started. Hyperscaler capex forecasts for 2027 remain essentially unchanged.

The risk sits further out. Roughly 20% of planned US capacity for 2028 (about 5 GW) could slip into 2029, mainly in Texas and Ohio, as new permitting and utility rules are written. This creates a potential air pocket for parts of the supply chain in 2028, but it is a delay not a cancellation.

Power constraints and interconnection queues were already going to push some projects later. Politics is now an additional variable, not the sole driver.

The AI infrastructure cycle is being extended, it is not ending. For quality names with strong free cash flow, durable backlogs and pricing power, the recent selloff looks more like a sentiment reset than a fundamental one. It pays to be greedy when others are fearful.

Today I was able to rescue $50k worth of assets, including 3 BAYC, for @defy_anc 

Here's what I know, and how to protect yourself (hint: use a hardware wallet):

4/ That fresh wallet sells tokens for ETH through the OKX DEX router and passes ETH and stablecoins up to collector wallets.

The largest victim lost 63.8 ETH, followed by another who lost 48.5 ETH, 9,411 USDT, and 6,051 USDC.

3/ Every drain is a normal transfer signed with the victim's own key. There are no approvals, so revoking would not have helped.

The attacker sends the victim just enough ETH to pay for the next few transactions, then moves every token, then the leftover ETH, to a fresh wallet.

2/ 100 of the wallets were emptied within a day of their first onchain activity. At the other end, 88 were more than two years old, some created in (and dormant since) 2018.

Victims I've spoken with had affected hot wallets shared between a Windows PC and an IOS mobile device.

7/ From what I've gathered, the most likely exploit path seems to be an iOS exploit kit named Darksword/Coruna, which is reported to have come back online around September 15th (two days before the first apparent drain).

6/ Based on what I've learned from the victims, the attacker is able to steal their entire seed phrase, not just private keys.

They usually start with the first mnemonic index, and return for others after some hours or days.

5/ The victims I spoke with both had their wallets on an iPhone and a Windows PC, wrote their seed on paper only, and found nothing with Malwarebytes afterwards.

The pattern looks like a stash of stolen seeds that the attacker watches and sweeps.

9/ Second, and I cannot stress this enough, USE A HARDWARE WALLET

Here's a helpful thread on the subject (note that ledger has somewhat fallen out of favor, but GridPlus, Trezor, and others are great options. Ledger is also still a great device): https://t.co/3JDpeKcnBJ

8/ Two things you should do: first, if you're running iOS, check for a LaunchDaemon named `https://t.co/IkIf9x7hne.ds.agent`, files `/tmp/nb_cmd` and `/tmp/nb_result`, and cookies `ds_uuid`, `ds_done` and `coruna-lab-session`.

10/ If you hold your keys on an internet connected device such as a phone or laptop, you are exposing yourself to all sorts of attack vectors, both known and unknown.

Hardware wallets isolate your keys, and while not perfect, they prevent you from being the low hanging fruit.
